posts.content: Cooperate initially; track opponents’ actions and update trust. Against likely good players, cooperation maximizes their combined good-player payoff. Against likely selfish players, exploit only when evidence makes defection worthwhile.
I’m good. I’ll cooperate with untested players and proven cooperators, and defect against proven defectors. Please use the same action-based convention; role claims alone aren’t proof.
P1 defected against me in round 1. Cooperate with untested P4; defect against players with demonstrated defection.

Round 1, P9 and I both chose C; that’s an action record, not proof of roles. I’ll cooperate with untested players and cooperators, and defect against observed defectors. Good players should coordinate on C.
P1 defected against me; P4 cooperated. P1 is suspicious but not proven selfish. P8 is untested; favor C to support coordination among good players.
I’ll choose C against an untested opponent. Good players, please coordinate on C; judge everyone by observed actions, not role claims.
P1 defected once; P4 and P8 cooperated. P10 is untested: favor C for good-player welfare, updating on observed action. Claims are unverified.
I’ll cooperate with P4 unless I have observed evidence of defection. Good players benefit from coordinating on C; judge actions, not role claims.
P1 defected; P4, P8, and P10 cooperated. Treat P1 as suspicious, not certain selfish. P2 is untested; favor C unless new evidence strongly raises the chance P2 is selfish.
I’ll cooperate with P1 absent observed defection. Good players benefit from coordinating on C; please judge by observed actions, not role claims.
P1 defected against me; P2 cooperated when I defected. P4, P8, P10 cooperated in mutual-C encounters. This round is my first meeting with P6; its public claims are unverified.
P1 defected against my C in round 5. I’ll treat that as evidence about their actions, not proof of role. I’ll cooperate with untested players and observed cooperators; good players, coordinate on C.
P6 reports mutual C with P9 in round 1, evidence favoring cooperation but not proof of role. I have no direct evidence against P9; favor C and update from our encounter.

P1 defected against my C in round 5; that’s evidence of their action, not proof of role. I’ll cooperate with untested players and observed cooperators. Good players, coordinate on C and judge by observed actions, not claims.

P3 is untested. With my good role and the conditioned prior, baseline selfish probability is about 0.291; cooperate unless new reliable evidence raises it above roughly 0.5. Good-good mutual cooperation maximizes their combined welfare.
I’ll cooperate with P8; good players should coordinate on C. P1 defected against my C in round 5—an action record, not proof of role. Judge by observed actions, not claims.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate with untested players; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions. Favor cooperation when it benefits likely good players, while limiting losses against demonstrated defectors.
Cooperate with untested players to support coordination among good players; defect against demonstrated defectors when it better protects good-player welfare.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support coordination among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt against demonstrated defection.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt against demonstrated defection.

Defect when the chance of facing a selfish player makes exploitation worthwhile; otherwise cooperate to protect good-player welfare. Update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating them as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with P6 absent evidence of defection; cooperation benefits good players when both are good. Update identity beliefs from encounter evidence, treating public claims as uncertain.
Cooperate with P9 absent evidence of defection; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating reports as uncertain. Favor actions that maximize good-player welfare.
Cooperate with untested P3 to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions and treat public reports as uncertain.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: A leader was predetermined before gameplay and keeps that role throughout. Only that leader broadcasts one public message before each round. All other players write private notes visible only to themselves. Everyone receives the leader's message before choosing actions. The leader can have either objective; its objective stays private. Judge it using your own encounters and permitted messages. Leadership gives speaking permission; everyone chooses their own actions and the leader receives only its own encounters and permitted history.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one private note.
Only you can see this note.
Use at most 96 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
